summary: Two one-thread T0 runs reproduced every deterministic field. Centralized and distributed trainable gradients, clipped gradients, AdamW state, complete model state, loss, routing, and frozen-head identity matched exactly. Four cold expert workers used 13,144,064 tensor bytes round trip, 7.34% above the matched cold full control. After both paths retained the same immutable 2,098,176-byte head, warm expert traffic used 4,751,360 bytes, 53.17% below the matched warm full control.

guardrails.detail: Maximum centralized-to-distributed raw-gradient, clipped-gradient, and complete-model differences were 0.0; paired gradient, optimizer, and model SHA-256 values matched.
The initial, centralized-final, and distributed-final head SHA-256 was d559917a27b24b83058a15e7427b745bd96c11ae0eb370be9c84ebf175d49fd7, with zero gradient bytes and zero optimizer-state parameters.

Cold controls include the frozen head in model download. Warm controls retain the same 2,098,176 head bytes and refresh all trainable parameters; both include their exact gradient uploads and input traffic.
Primary and repeat records matched in every field except centralized/distributed elapsed seconds and combined-process peak RSS.

findings.label: Frozen-head expert decomposition is exact
findings.description: Removing head trainability did not break exact mapping of router, shared-trunk, or expert gradients into one coordinator-owned AdamW update.

findings.label: Warm aggregate traffic is materially lower
findings.description: With the same immutable head retained by both paths, four experts used 53.17% fewer accounted tensor bytes than the full sparse control.

findings.label: Cold fan-out remains more expensive
findings.description: Duplicating the head across four newly initialized workers left the cold expert round trip 7.34% above the matched full control.

findings.label: The warm result is accounting, not process evidence
findings.description: This control justifies the next authenticated T1 process experiment; it does not prove cache reuse, memory, latency, reliability, or model quality in that environment.

limitations: The model is randomly initialized T0, the data is synthetic, and the run has one optimizer step; no useful model behavior or training quality is established.
Workers are local objects in one process. Authentication, process isolation, network transfer, cache persistence across assignments, restart, and retry are not executed.
Tensor traffic is exact accounting, not packet-level measurement. Serialization, protocol headers, compression, and transport latency are excluded.
The warm comparison gives both paths the same immutable-head cache and refreshes every trainable tensor after coordinator AdamW. Other cache or delta-update policies may change the result.
Capacity routing forced 128 tokens to every expert by rerouting 44 of 512 tokens. The measured balance is policy intervention, not learned specialization.
Elapsed time and combined-process peak RSS are observational and differ between the two runs.
